spend-change.answer:
## Spending in 2025 vs 2024

Spending rose sharply, but a small number of very large invoices drives most of the increase. Counting invoices by `invoice_date`:

| Metric | 2024 | 2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| GBP invoice spend | £33,740,836,486.87 | £91,777,234,483.22 | +£58,036,397,996 (+172%) |
| GBP invoice count | 14,177 | 13,253 | −924 (−6.5%) |
| GBP average invoice | £2,379,970 | £6,925,016 | +191% |
| GBP median invoice | £30,789 | £39,174 | +27% |
| Invoices over £100M | 52 (£25.45B) | 152 (£79.78B) | +100 invoices, +£54.3B |
| Spend excluding invoices over £100M | £8.29B (14,125 invoices) | £12.00B (13,101 invoices) | +£3.71B (+44.7%) |

**What changed:**
- Volume fell slightly, but the average and median invoice grew, so the value per invoice went up.
- Invoices over £100M went from 52 to 152, and their share of GBP spend rose from about 75% to about 87%.
- Excluding those large invoices, spend still grew about 45%, so the rise is not only from the outliers.

**Other currencies (small):**
- EUR: 5 invoices (€5.24M) in 2024 and 2 invoices (€0.91M) in 2025.
- USD: 1 invoice each year ($49,332.99 in 2024 and $61,591.51 in 2025).

**Assumptions and caveats:**
- Spend is the sum of invoice `amount` by `invoice_date`, not payments made. Amounts are shown in their invoice currency and are not converted.
- Single invoices of several billion pounds (the largest is about £5.75B in 2025) look implausible for real procurement. This may be a data-quality issue in the synthetic dataset. Verify the largest invoices before relying on the headline growth figure.

**Sources:** SQL on `invoices` (grouped by year and currency, plus a GBP breakdown with a £100M threshold), and `run_metric: total_spend` by month for cross-checking.

args.sql: SELECT payment_status, status, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(due_date) AS min_due, MAX(due_date) AS max_due FROM invoices GROUP BY payment_status, status ORDER BY n DESC

SELECT v.name AS vendor, COUNT(*) AS overdue_invoices, ROUND(SUM(i.amount)::numeric, 2) AS overdue_amount, i.currency, MIN(i.due_date) AS oldest_due FROM invoices i JOIN vendors v ON v.id = i.vendor_id WHERE i.status = 'overdue' GROUP BY v.name, i.currency ORDER BY overdue_invoices DESC, overdue_amount DESC LIMIT 15

SELECT UPPER(v.name) AS vendor, COUNT(*) AS overdue_invoices, ROUND(SUM(i.amount)::numeric, 2) AS overdue_amount_gbp, MIN(i.due_date) AS oldest_due, COUNT(DISTINCT v.id) AS name_variants FROM invoices i JOIN vendors v ON v.id = i.vendor_id WHERE i.status = 'overdue' GROUP BY UPPER(v.name) ORDER BY overdue_invoices DESC, overdue_amount_gbp DESC LIMIT 10
